notes: Portfolio mix, in Planning › Insights: what your investments are made of, against a common guide for your age, with tips to balance it
Tips cover too much or too little in the market, no gold, one investment carrying too much, high-yield bonds, a short emergency fund, steady income near retirement and money locked till retirement
Each tip suggests options to look at, such as listed bonds, government bonds, debt funds, gold ETFs, REITs, Post Office and senior citizens' schemes, with returns, risk, minimums and cautions
Portfolio tips appear in For you today on Home, with the most pressing one shown every day
Investments links to your mix with its top tip
Goal planning opens with your plan at a glance: the extra needed a month, goals on track, what's set aside and retirement, then tabs for Goals and Retirement
Goals show as cards with a progress bar and the next step, and each goal's details open full screen with its figures as cards
Retirement leads with when your money runs out, a timeline of working, retired and any years not covered, ways to close a gap as cards, and one chart at a time
Your assumptions are grouped into You, Spending, Investing and After you retire, with the key numbers shown when folded
Set each investment: each shows what it does after you retire, and opens to edit with a plain explanation, how it pays, then the amount
The bottom tab bar is solid, and content fades out above it instead of showing through
Payouts that vary, such as a profit share or dividends, can be set up with just how often they come; Home asks for the amount each time, and it's added to income and counted in returns
